slides.title: Welcome

kind.alt: A smiling warehouse worker in a hi-vis vest holds a tablet beside shelves of boxes.

kind.text: Most workplace injuries start with something small. Learn to spot three everyday hazards and the habit that stops each one.

slides.notes: The course opens here. About this course opens a layer with what to expect.

kind.text: A short course for anyone who works in a shop, a warehouse or an office.
About 5 minutes, at your own pace
Three hazards, each with one simple habit
Four graded questions. You need 75% to pass

slides.title: Three everyday hazards
slides.notes: Each tab shows one hazard on its own layer. The selected tab keeps its Selected state.

kind.alt: A worker steps over a loose cable and an open box left on the floor.

kind.text: Cables, boxes and open drawers in a walkway catch your feet when you are busy.

kind.alt: A worker squats with a straight back to lift a box from the floor.

kind.text: Lifting with a bent back strains it. Your legs are much stronger.
Bend your knees, not your back

kind.alt: A wet floor sign and a mop bucket stand beside a puddle in a corridor.

kind.text: A small puddle near a door is easy to miss and easy to slip on.
Put out a wet floor sign
Clean it up or report it

slides.title: Spot the hazards

kind.alt: A workshop with a tall unsteady stack of boxes, a loose cable across the floor and a puddle under a table.

kind.text: Tip: select a marker again to move it.

slides.notes: A hotspot question with three markers. Each marker must land on a hazard.

question.prompt: Find the three hazards. Place a marker on each one.

kind.text: Well spotted! Boxes stacked high, a loose cable and a puddle.
Not all of your markers are on a hazard. Look again at the floor and the stack.

kind.alt: A wet floor sign and a mop bucket beside a puddle.

question.prompt: You notice water on the floor near a busy doorway. What should you do first?

choices.text: Walk around it carefully and carry on
Warn people nearby and put out a wet floor sign
Wait until the end of your shift to report it

kind.text: Right. Warn people first, then clean it up or report it.
Not quite. Someone could slip before it is dealt with.

kind.alt: A worker lifting a box with bent knees.

question.prompt: Which of these make lifting a box safer? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Bend your knees and keep your back straight
Twist your body to turn while you lift
Hold the box close to your body
Test the weight before you lift

kind.text: Exactly. Bent knees, a close load and a quick test lift.
Not quite. Twisting while you lift strains your back.

kind.alt: A loose cable across a walkway.

question.prompt: You find a cable across a walkway. Put these steps in the right order.

choices.text: Stop and warn anyone walking past
Unplug the cable if it is safe to do so
Reroute it or cover it with a cable protector
Report it so it is fixed for good

kind.text: Well done. Warn, make safe, fix, then report.
Not quite. Think about keeping people safe first.

slides.title: Your result
slides.notes: Submits the quiz on start, then shows the passed or failed layer.

kind.text: Keep walkways clear, lift with your legs and deal with spills straight away.
You need 75% to pass. Review the three hazards and try the questions again.
